title: Android Implant Investigation
description: Investigate a compromise by the HackingTeam Android implant on the victim host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has been compromised by an Android implant known as HackingTeam. This spyware is capable of data exfiltration, screen recording, audio recording, and executing code from downloaded dex files. Your task is to investigate the compromise, identify the indicators of compromise (IOCs), and contain the threat. The flags you need to find include the name of a suspicious systemd timer, the path to a captured keystroke log file, and the path to a data exfiltration script.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the victim host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The victim host's IP address is `192.168.100.10`. To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the victim host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The victim host's IP address is `192.168.100.10`. To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious scheduled task/timer used for data collection
levels.content: Investigate the systemd timers on the victim host to identify any suspicious scheduled tasks that might be related to the spyware. The flag is the name of the suspicious timer.
levels.solution: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers. Look for any timers that are not part of the standard system configuration. The suspicious timer is likely named `com.google.android.MainService.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers.

levels.title: Identify the captured keystroke log file
levels.content: Search the victim host for any files that might contain captured keystrokes. These files could be used by the spyware to exfiltrate sensitive information. The flag is the path to the captured keystroke log file.
levels.solution: Check directories and files that are not typically part of the system configuration. The captured keystroke log file is likely located at `/var/lib/.monitor/keylog.log`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check directories and files that are not typically part of the system configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: The captured keystroke log file is likely located at `/var/lib/.monitor/keylog.log`.

levels.title: Identify the data exfiltration mechanism
levels.content: Investigate the network communication on the victim host to identify any suspicious outbound connections that might be used for data exfiltration. The flag is the path to the data exfiltration script.
levels.solution: Look for connections to unexpected IP addresses or ports. The data exfiltration mechanism is likely the script located at `/usr/local/lib/.monitor/exfil.sh`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for connections to unexpected IP addresses or ports.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: The data exfiltration mechanism is likely the script located at `/usr/local/lib/.monitor/exfil.sh`.
